page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM, equivalent to 3.75 GB of memory per core. The underlying hardware is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 45 MB of L3 cache. The CPU supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place the n1-standard-8 primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, register in the weak to poor categories. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds are rated as poor. However, memory performance is relatively stronger; while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks achieve average ratings. Passmark memory scores and Geekbench ray tracing tests also reach average performance levels, whereas database operations and static web serving throughput remain in the weak tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for legacy general-purpose workloads that do not require high-frequency compute or modern AVX-512 instructions. Given the lack of local storage and moderate CPU performance, it is best suited for workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, or lightweight background processing tasks where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
